_doc: GROUNDED still specs — the fix for lazy/repetitive prompting. Each still is derived from its NARRATION beat + a cited Bible verse-detail, given a DISTINCT shot_type + a subject_signature (for dedup), a pinned arm/hand position for any Christ figure (kills the recurring prayer-hand-from-chest default), and a distinct_from note vs its former look-alike. still_validate.py checks this file BEFORE any render: duplicate signatures, over-repeated shot_type, missing verse grounding, biblical-accuracy rule hits, prayer-hand guard, poison tokens.

poured_out_bones.verse: Psalm 22:14 — I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint
poured_out_bones.arms: both nailed wide overhead, wrenched taut
poured_out_bones.distinct_from: bones_wasted_body (that is a rib MACRO, no figure) and convergence_on_cross (front symmetric)
poured_out_bones.prompt: a dramatic LOW-ANGLE looking steeply UP the cross of Christ ({CH}) from the ground, his full weight dragging DOWN so both arms are stretched wide and taut along the horizontal crossbeam and the shoulders pull from their sockets, each hand open and flat against the beam far apart with a dark pierced wound in the centre of each open palm, head fallen back against the black sky; the strained dislocated joints are the clear focus; reverent, 1st-century

pierced_feet.verse: Psalm 22:16 — they pierced my hands and my feet
pierced_feet.distinct_from: pierced_hands_feet (that is the pierced HAND) — this is the feet, one nail per foot
pierced_feet.prompt: a close view of two bare feet set side by side flat on a rough wooden beam, a separate long slender iron crucifixion nail driven straight down through EACH foot — two nails, one per foot — each with only a small nail-head showing flush on the skin and a thin shaft going into the wood, dark blood welling around each puncture and running down the grain; plain thin spikes, reverent, 1st-century

greek_ot_scroll.verse: the Septuagint (Greek OT) already read 'they pierced', translated by Jewish scholars ~2 centuries before Christ
greek_ot_scroll.distinct_from: scribe_over_manuscripts (a lone scribe writing), disputed_word_marks (a macro of one mark), two_scrolls_compared (two scrolls) — this is a WIDE scene of scholars translating
greek_ot_scroll.prompt: inside a dim ancient Hellenistic-era library lit ONLY by a few small flickering clay oil lamps with warm uneven flame-light and deep pooling shadows, several Jewish scholars in period Judean robes bent together over a long unrolled papyrus scroll, gesturing in discussion as they translate it, shelves stacked with rolled scrolls fading into darkness behind them; the scroll surface only soft indistinct texture with no legible letters; ancient scholarship centuries before the cross; antiquity

risen_hands_raised.verse: Psalm 22:24 — when he cried unto him, he heard (answered)
risen_hands_raised.arms: both open hands raised only to shoulder height, healed scar in each palm
risen_hands_raised.distinct_from: risen_worshipper (WIDE, among a congregation) — this is an intimate close of the face, no crowd
risen_hands_raised.prompt: a CLOSE intimate view of the risen Christ ({CH}) with face lifted and eyes gently lowered in deep peace, both open hands raised only to shoulder height, a single closed healed scar flat in the centre of each palm, bathed in soft warm light, entirely alone and serene, no crowd; the quiet of answered prayer; 1st-century

nations_streaming_wide.verse: Psalm 22:27 — all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee
nations_streaming_wide.distinct_from: ends_of_earth (a ground-level multitude flowing to a cross) — this is a bird's-eye of converging roads emphasising national diversity
nations_streaming_wide.prompt: a sweeping BIRD'S-EYE view of many roads winding across the whole land inward from every distant horizon, each road crowded with peoples of visibly different nations and dress, all converging toward one hill of warm light at the centre; the diversity of the streaming kindreds is the subject; epic, dawn light

kneeling_at_cross.verse: the personal invitation — the forsaking fell on him so it would never fall on you
kneeling_at_cross.distinct_from: parting_storm_light (a WIDE atmospheric cross as the storm parts) — this is an intimate ground-level shot of upturned faces
kneeling_at_cross.prompt: a low view looking UP a single rough wooden cross that TOWERS tall and fills the height of the frame, three small kneeling figures gathered tiny at its base far below, dwarfed by the great height of the cross above them, warm breaking light behind; correct monumental scale, the cross vast and the people small; 1st-century

hand_reaching_closeup.verse: the CTA — come and join the ones who praise him (the reaching, scarred hand)
hand_reaching_closeup.arms: one open right hand, healed scar centre-palm, filling the frame
hand_reaching_closeup.distinct_from: risen_hero_come (a FULL risen figure reaching) — this is an extreme macro of ONLY the hand, no face
hand_reaching_closeup.prompt: an EXTREME close-up of a single open right hand filling the entire frame, reaching straight toward the viewer out of warm golden light, a single closed healed scar in the very centre of the open palm, fingers spread in open invitation; only the hand — no face, no body; inviting, personal; 1st-century

david_hands_lyre.verse: Psalm 22 authorship — David wrote it first-person, as his own body
david_hands_lyre.arms: both weathered hands cradling and plucking the lyre strings
david_hands_lyre.distinct_from: david_psalmist (a wide of David seated singing) — this is close over the shoulder onto the playing hands
david_hands_lyre.prompt: a close OVER-THE-SHOULDER view onto the aged shepherd-king David's weathered hands cradling and plucking the strings of a wooden lyre by warm lamplight, his singing profile just visible beyond, the strings catching the light; Iron-Age Israelite; 1st-millennium-BC

mocker_faces_trio.verse: Psalm 22:7 — they shoot out the lip, they shake the head
mocker_faces_trio.distinct_from: mockers_wag_heads (a wide knot at the foot of the cross) — this is a tight trio of cruel faces
mocker_faces_trio.prompt: three DISTINCTLY DIFFERENT 1st-century men close in the foreground sneering with cruel contempt at someone below — one old and gaunt with a long grey beard, one broad and heavy-jowled, one lean and young with a thin beard — each a clearly different face, lips curled back, teeth bared in derision, cold hostile eyes, a dark blurred crowd behind; dusty earth tones; antiquity

lots_dice_closeup.verse: Psalm 22:18 / John 19:24 — they cast lots upon my vesture
lots_dice_closeup.arms: rough soldiers' hands casting the lots
lots_dice_closeup.distinct_from: crane_cross_soldiers (a wide down the cross to the soldiers) — this is a macro of the lots themselves
lots_dice_closeup.prompt: a close OVER-THE-SHOULDER macro of rough Roman soldiers' hands casting small carved animal knucklebones onto a folded seamless robe on the stony ground; dusty, warm hard light; 1st-century

scholar_hand_on_text.verse: the honest objection — a genuine scholarly dispute over the word 'pierced'
scholar_hand_on_text.arms: one hand hovering thoughtfully over the parchment
scholar_hand_on_text.distinct_from: scribe_over_manuscripts (a scribe writing) — this is a scholar pausing to weigh a difficulty
scholar_hand_on_text.prompt: a CLOSE view of a thoughtful bearded Near-Eastern scholar pausing over a spread parchment by lamplight, his brow furrowed in honest doubt, one hand hovering above the text as he weighs a difficulty, the parchment only soft indistinct texture; antiquity, period robes

two_scrolls_compared.verse: the disputed word — two textual readings set against each other
two_scrolls_compared.distinct_from: greek_ot_scroll (a wide translation scene) — this is a top-down of two texts side by side
two_scrolls_compared.prompt: a HIGH top-down view of two aged parchment scrolls unrolled side by side on a dark wooden table in warm lamplight, one older and darker than the other, their surfaces only soft indistinct texture; the quiet comparison of two texts; antiquity

cross_hill_pullback.verse: back to the cross — why that cry matters
cross_hill_pullback.distinct_from: storm_over_jerusalem (the city + three crosses) — this is a single stark cross wide on the hill
cross_hill_pullback.prompt: a WIDE establishing view of a single rough wooden cross standing stark on a rocky hill under a vast brooding sky, small against the land, one pale shaft of light breaking onto it from the torn clouds; epic, 1st-century

face_anguish_closeup.verse: Psalm 22:1 — the forsaken cry, as Jesus claims the whole psalm
face_anguish_closeup.distinct_from: cry_face_tears (a quiet single tear, eyes lowered) — this is the open-mouthed SHOUT, eyes flung to heaven
face_anguish_closeup.prompt: an extreme CLOSE-UP of the crucified Christ's ({CH}) face flung upward and mouth wide open in a full-throated cry to heaven, brow knotted, the tendons of the neck taut, a hard shaft of light across the face; the shout is the subject; reverent, 1st-century

cry_face_tears.verse: Psalm 22:15 — brought into the dust of death (the killing thirst)
cry_face_tears.distinct_from: face_anguish_closeup (an open-mouthed shout) — this is quiet: parched cracked lips, a single tear, eyes half-lowered
cry_face_tears.prompt: an extreme CLOSE-UP of the crucified Christ's ({CH}) face gone quiet in the dust of death, the lips cracked and parched, the eyes half-lowered and glazed, a single tear tracking through the grime, the head sunk low; a shaft of light across the face; restrained, reverent, 1st-century

worm_lowest.verse: Psalm 22:6 — But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men
worm_lowest.arms: both arms hanging limp at his sides
worm_lowest.distinct_from: the crucified stills — this figure is NOT on the cross: a stripped man bowed and broken with reproach
worm_lowest.prompt: the suffering Christ ({CH}) stripped to a plain loincloth, standing bowed and broken with head hung low and shoulders sunk, both arms hanging limp at his sides, utterly despised and alone in deep shadow; dark, 1st-century

empty_tomb_open.verse: the turn — the song does not end in a grave; it turns from death to life
empty_tomb_open.distinct_from: storm/cross stills — this is the dark interior of the emptied tomb, no figure
empty_tomb_open.prompt: inside a dark empty rock-hewn tomb chamber, a bare stone burial ledge with folded white linen grave-cloths resting on it, a soft shaft of pale dawn light falling across the empty ledge from the open entrance; still, hopeful, 1st-century

dogs_encompass.verse: Psalm 22:16a — For dogs have compassed me (narration: 'vivid images — dogs, a lion')
dogs_encompass.distinct_from: mockers_wag_heads (human mockers) — this is the psalm's animal image: wild dogs circling at night
dogs_encompass.prompt: a GROUND-LEVEL night view of a pack of lean wild dogs circling in a tightening ring around a bare patch of moonlit stony ground, every animal fully canine with heavy four-toed canine forepaws planted in the dust, eyes catching the pale light as the ring closes inward; ancient Judean wilderness menace; 1st-millennium-BC

lion_gape.verse: Psalm 22:13 — they gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion
lion_gape.distinct_from: dogs_encompass (a circling pack, wide) — this is one great lion head, close, mid-roar
lion_gape.prompt: a CLOSE view of a great lion mid-roar in deep shadow, wild mane, jaws gaping wide with the teeth catching one hard sliver of light, hot breath hazing in the cold air; raw ancient menace; 1st-millennium-BC

hung_by_arms.verse: Psalm 22:14 — all my bones are out of joint (narration: 'a man hung up by his arms — the joints pulling apart under his own weight')
hung_by_arms.arms: both arms stretched high and taut overhead to the crossbeam, the body sagging from the wrists
hung_by_arms.distinct_from: poured_out_bones (a lit low-angle figure with a visible face) — this is a stark backlit SILHOUETTE, no facial detail at all
hung_by_arms.prompt: a stark SILHOUETTE against a bruised storm sky: the pure black shape of a man hanging on a cross, both arms stretched high and taut to the crossbeam, the whole body sagging heavily downward from the wrists so the shoulders wrench upward, ragged torn clouds behind; the dragging weight is the subject; 1st-century

garment_tug.verse: John 19:24 / Psalm 22:18 — they parted my raiment among them (soldiers gambling for a dead man's clothes)
garment_tug.arms: two soldiers' rough fists gripping opposite ends of the folded robe
garment_tug.distinct_from: lots_dice_closeup (the knucklebones being cast) — this is the ROBE itself pulled taut between two fists
garment_tug.prompt: a tight view of two Roman soldiers' rough fists gripping opposite ends of a folded seamless woven robe, pulling it taut between them above a scatter of small carved knucklebones on the stony ground, dust hanging in the hard light; the tug-of-war over the garment is the subject; 1st-century

first_century_reader.verse: the first verse pulling the entire psalm into the room — how a first-century Jew quoted Scripture
first_century_reader.arms: one hand lifted as he recites, the other steadying the unrolled scroll
first_century_reader.distinct_from: greek_ot_scroll (scholars translating at a table) and scribe_over_manuscripts (a lone scribe writing) — this is a reader RECITING ALOUD to listeners
first_century_reader.prompt: a 1st-century Judean man standing in a small stone synagogue holding an unrolled scroll, one hand lifted as he recites aloud from memory, a few seated listeners leaning in around him in warm lamplight, the scroll surface only soft indistinct texture; the spoken word filling the room; 1st-century

vinegar_sponge.verse: John 19:29-30 — he receives the vinegar (just before 'It is finished')
vinegar_sponge.arms: a single arm lifting the long reed upward
vinegar_sponge.distinct_from: pierced_hands_feet / pierced_feet (the wounds) — this is the offered sponge on the reed, no figure on the cross visible
vinegar_sponge.prompt: a LOW view up into a darkening sky: a single bare arm lifting a long reed with a soaked sponge bound at its tip, raised up toward the rough wood of a cross edging into the top of the frame, drops falling back against the failing light; the offered vinegar is the subject; 1st-century

dawn_empty_cross.verse: the hinge — the cross was never the end of the song (the turn from death to life)
dawn_empty_cross.distinct_from: cross_hill_pullback (a brooding grey storm wide) — this is DAWN: the storm rolling away, warm gold flooding the land
dawn_empty_cross.prompt: a WIDE view of a single rough wooden cross on its rocky hill at DAWN, the storm rolling away behind it and warm gold light flooding across the land from the horizon, long soft shadows and a clearing sky; the hinge from night to morning; 1st-century

kindreds_bowing.verse: Psalm 22:27 — all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee
kindreds_bowing.distinct_from: nations_streaming_wide (a bird's-eye of converging roads) and ends_of_earth (a multitude flowing to the cross) — this is a RING of worshippers already arrived, bowing low together
kindreds_bowing.prompt: a wide view of a great ring of worshippers from visibly many nations in the varied dress of distant ancient lands, all bowing low together toward a warm rising light at the centre of the frame, robes of many colours, faces hidden in reverence; the bowed circle of the kindreds is the subject; epic dawn

golgotha_three_crosses_ridge.verse: the witness statement from a cross (Ps 22 read forensically)
golgotha_three_crosses_ridge.prompt: a GROUND-LEVEL view across dark scrubland to a low ridge where three crosses stand small and stark against a vast bruised storm sky, one shaft of cold light striking the middle cross; epic emptiness; 1st-century
golgotha_three_crosses_ridge.distinct_from: storm_over_jerusalem (city+temple wide) and cross_hill_pullback (single cross) - this is THREE crosses tiny on a ridge

ninth_hour_darkness.verse: Matthew 27:45 - darkness over the land at the ninth hour
ninth_hour_darkness.prompt: a WIDE view over flat-roofed 1st-century Jerusalem houses and square Herodian stone watchtowers as an unnatural darkness swallows the midday sun, a dim ring of light in a black-green sky, birds scattering; dread; 1st-century
ninth_hour_darkness.distinct_from: storm_over_jerusalem (temple + crosses) - this is the DARKENED SUN over rooftops, no cross

roman_nails_pouch.arms: a soldier's hand tipping the pouch
roman_nails_pouch.prompt: a MACRO of a worn leather pouch tipped by a soldier's rough hand, long slender iron nails with small square heads spilling out across a flat stone in hard light; plain thin spikes; 1st-century
roman_nails_pouch.distinct_from: pierced_hands_feet (a nail IN a hand) - these are loose nails spilling from a pouch

david_scroll_sealed.arms: one ringed hand pressing a clay seal
david_scroll_sealed.prompt: a MACRO of an aged royal hand with a signet ring pressing a small clay seal onto the tie of a freshly rolled papyrus scroll by lamplight, the papyrus surface only soft indistinct texture; 1st-millennium-BC
david_scroll_sealed.distinct_from: two_scrolls_compared (two open scrolls) - this is ONE rolled scroll being SEALED

jerusalem_night_lyre.verse: David composing under the night sky
jerusalem_night_lyre.prompt: a WIDE moonlit view of ancient stone rooftops and a city wall, one small distant figure seated on a high rooftop corner with a lyre against the starfield; lonely and quiet; 1st-millennium-BC
jerusalem_night_lyre.distinct_from: david_psalmist (close, face visible) - this is a tiny DISTANT figure in a wide night city

execution_stakes_field.verse: a public execution (the death David describes)
execution_stakes_field.prompt: a WIDE bleak view in muted warm earth colors of a rocky execution ground outside a pale stone city wall, several empty upright wooden stakes and crossbeams against a heavy grey-gold sky, dark birds circling far off; dread, no figures; cel-flat color; 1st-century
execution_stakes_field.distinct_from: golgotha_three_crosses_ridge (three crosses on a ridge) - this is an EMPTY execution ground of bare stakes

mockers_below_cross_low.verse: Psalm 22:8 - the mockers' taunt hurled up at the cross
mockers_below_cross_low.arms: one mocker's arm flung up in derision
mockers_below_cross_low.prompt: an OVER-THE-SHOULDER view from behind two jeering men in 1st-century robes, one arm flung up in derision, looking steeply UP toward the crucified figure high on the cross against the dark sky above them; hostile energy below, stillness above; 1st-century
mockers_below_cross_low.distinct_from: mockers_wag_heads (frontal faces w/ Christ small centre) - this is from BEHIND the mockers looking UP

spit_shout_macro.verse: Psalm 22:7 - they shoot out the lip (the jeer itself)
spit_shout_macro.prompt: a hard CLOSE profile of one 1st-century man mid-jeer, lip curled and teeth bared, spittle flecks catching the light against a dark blurred crowd; ugly contempt; 1st-century
spit_shout_macro.distinct_from: mocker_faces_trio (three faces frontal) - this is ONE jeering profile, extreme close

old_king_hands_rings.verse: a king who died of old age (contrast with the psalm's death)
old_king_hands_rings.arms: two aged hands at rest on a woven blanket
old_king_hands_rings.prompt: a MACRO of two aged royal hands at rest on a woven blanket, gold rings loose on thin fingers, warm lamplight, utterly peaceful; a safe death; 1st-millennium-BC
old_king_hands_rings.distinct_from: david_old_deathbed (the wide deathbed scene) - this is only the resting HANDS

shepherd_boy_sling.verse: David the soldier-king's real life (never executed)
shepherd_boy_sling.arms: one hand swinging a leather sling at his side
shepherd_boy_sling.prompt: a FULL-FIGURE view of a young shepherd on a green hillside among sheep, a leather sling swinging loose from one hand, morning light; vigorous life; 1st-millennium-BC
shepherd_boy_sling.distinct_from: david_psalmist (the aged singer) - this is YOUNG David the shepherd

war_helmet_spear_rest.verse: a soldier and a king (his battles ended in peace)
war_helmet_spear_rest.prompt: a MACRO of an old dented bronze helmet and a tall spear leaned together against a stone wall by a bed, dust motes in a warm shaft of light; wars long over; 1st-millennium-BC
war_helmet_spear_rest.distinct_from: old_king_hands_rings (hands on blanket) - this is the retired WEAPONS by the wall

wrists_bound_beam_macro.verse: a man fixed to wood through his hands (Ps 22:16)
wrists_bound_beam_macro.arms: one wrist lashed and nailed to the rough beam, tendons taut
wrists_bound_beam_macro.prompt: a MACRO of a single forearm and wrist lashed with cord and nailed to a rough wooden beam, the tendons taut under the skin, a thin dark line of blood in the wood grain, storm light; no face; 1st-century
wrists_bound_beam_macro.distinct_from: pierced_hands_feet (open palm with nail) - this is the LASHED WRIST from the side, tendons straining

ribs_stretched_macro.verse: Psalm 22:14 - all my bones are out of joint
ribs_stretched_macro.prompt: a CLOSE side-lit view of a gaunt man's bare chest as he hangs with arms high out of frame, every rib pressing visibly through the taut skin as ridged lines of light and shadow, hard chiaroscuro; reverent, no face; 1st-century
ribs_stretched_macro.distinct_from: poured_out_bones (full low-angle figure) - this is ONLY the strained ribcage, side view

clay_potsherd_dust.verse: Psalm 22:15 - my strength is dried up like a potsherd
clay_potsherd_dust.prompt: a MACRO of a single cracked shard of dry clay pottery lying in pale dust, hairline cracks spreading, heat shimmer; utter dryness; 1st-century
clay_potsherd_dust.distinct_from: thirst_dust (the parched face) - this is the psalm's POTSHERD image itself, no figure

water_spilled_stone.verse: Psalm 22:14 - I am poured out like water
water_spilled_stone.prompt: a MACRO of clear water spilling from a tipped clay jar across worn flagstones, the thin sheet of water catching one line of light as it runs away into the cracks; loss; 1st-century
water_spilled_stone.distinct_from: poured_out_bones (the crucified figure) - this is the WATER image literal: a jar poured out

sponge_vinegar_jar.verse: John 19:29 - a vessel full of vinegar
sponge_vinegar_jar.prompt: a MACRO of a squat clay jar of dark vinegar with a rough dry sponge and a long reed lying beside it on stony ground, hard afternoon light; waiting; 1st-century
sponge_vinegar_jar.distinct_from: vinegar_sponge (the sponge lifted on the reed) - this is the jar and sponge on the GROUND, before

dice_cup_shadow.arms: one soldier's hand tipping the horn cup
dice_cup_shadow.prompt: a MACRO of a soldier's hand tipping a horn dice-cup, small carved knucklebones caught mid-fall above the stone, long hard shadows; the moment before they land; 1st-century
dice_cup_shadow.distinct_from: lots_dice_closeup (bones already cast on the robe) - this is the CUP TIPPING, bones mid-air

vesture_seamless_folded.prompt: a MACRO top-down of a single seamless woven robe folded in a neat square on stony ground, one small carved knucklebone resting on it, dust in the light; the prize of the lot; 1st-century
vesture_seamless_folded.distinct_from: garment_tug (fists pulling the robe) - this is the robe FOLDED and still, top-down

john_at_cross_foot.verse: John 19:35 - he that saw it bare record
john_at_cross_foot.arms: both hands clutched to his chest as he looks up
john_at_cross_foot.prompt: a FULL-FIGURE view in warm cel-flat dusk colors of a young 1st-century disciple standing at the foot of the towering cross, wind pulling at his cloak, both hands clutched to his chest as he looks steeply up, the cross base and lower beam framing him; the witness; 1st-century
john_at_cross_foot.distinct_from: kneeling_at_cross (tiny kneelers at the base) - this is ONE standing young witness, mid shot

scholars_debate_two.verse: a genuine scholarly dispute, honestly raised
scholars_debate_two.arms: one scholar's hand raised mid-point, the other's palm open on the table
scholars_debate_two.prompt: an INTERIOR view of two Near-Eastern scholars facing each other across a lamplit table stacked with rolled scrolls, one hand raised mid-argument, the other open in honest concession, warm flame light and deep shadow; respectful dispute; antiquity
scholars_debate_two.distinct_from: greek_ot_scroll (a row of translators) and scholar_hand_on_text (one scholar alone) - this is TWO scholars in face-to-face dispute

quill_ink_drop.verse: yet there it is, in ink, centuries early
quill_ink_drop.arms: one hand lifting the reed pen
quill_ink_drop.prompt: a MACRO of a hand lifting a reed pen from a small clay inkwell, one dark drop of ink falling back, lamplight glinting on the wet nib; the act of writing; antiquity
quill_ink_drop.distinct_from: disputed_word_marks (marks on parchment) - this is the PEN and the ink drop, no writing visible

hebrew_scroll_edge_light.verse: the traditional Hebrew text (the disputed reading)
hebrew_scroll_edge_light.prompt: a MACRO of the curling edge of an ancient darkened scroll lifting slightly in lamplight, the surface only soft indistinct texture, fibres and cracks catching the flame glow; age itself; antiquity
hebrew_scroll_edge_light.distinct_from: disputed_word_marks (a spread with marks) - this is only the curling EDGE of one ancient scroll

lion_shadow_wall.verse: Psalm 22:13 - as a ravening and a roaring lion
lion_shadow_wall.prompt: the huge SHADOW of a prowling lion cast across a torchlit mud-brick wall at night, the beast itself unseen, torch flame guttering low in the corner; menace implied; 1st-millennium-BC
lion_shadow_wall.distinct_from: lion_gape (the roaring head itself) - this is only the SHADOW on a wall

alexandria_harbor_night.verse: the Septuagint translated in Alexandria, two centuries before
alexandria_harbor_night.prompt: a WIDE dusk view of an ancient Mediterranean harbor city, moored ships and colonnaded quays, a great lighthouse tower with its fire burning against the last light; Hellenistic Egypt; antiquity
alexandria_harbor_night.distinct_from: storm_over_jerusalem (Jerusalem + temple) - this is the Greek HARBOR city with the lighthouse

seventy_scribes_lamps.prompt: an INTERIOR wide of a long Hellenistic hall where rows of Jewish scribes work at low tables, each under his own small oil lamp, dozens of warm points of light in the gloom, scroll surfaces only soft texture; the great translation; antiquity
seventy_scribes_lamps.distinct_from: greek_ot_scroll (a knot of scholars at one table) - this is ROWS of many scribes under many lamps

roads_converge_valley.verse: one disputed word does not carry it; the convergence does
roads_converge_valley.prompt: a HIGH view of five pale footpaths descending different dark hillsides and meeting at a single sunlit crossing point on the valley floor; the lines converge on one place; timeless ancient land
roads_converge_valley.distinct_from: nations_streaming_wide (crowded roads to a hill of light) - these are EMPTY paths converging in a valley

cry_profile_dark.verse: Matthew 27:46 - Jesus cried with a loud voice
cry_profile_dark.prompt: a stark SILHOUETTE profile of the crucified Christ's head thrown back mid-cry against a black sky, one hard rim of cold light tracing the brow, open mouth and beard, all else darkness; the cry itself; 1st-century
cry_profile_dark.distinct_from: cry_ninth_hour (lit full figure) and face_anguish_closeup (lit frontal face) - this is a black rim-lit PROFILE

synagogue_listeners_lean.verse: how a first-century Jew heard a psalm quoted
synagogue_listeners_lean.prompt: an INTERIOR of a small stone synagogue where seated listeners lean forward into the lamplight toward an unseen reader, rapt weathered faces half-lit, deep warm shadow behind; the pull of the word; 1st-century
synagogue_listeners_lean.distinct_from: first_century_reader (the reader himself) - this is the LISTENERS leaning toward him

hill_crowd_watching_storm.verse: out loud, in front of witnesses
hill_crowd_watching_storm.prompt: a WIDE view of a dark ring of onlookers gathered on a slope beneath a swirling storm sky, all faces turned toward a distant lit rise where a cross stands small, dust blowing through; the watching crowd; 1st-century
hill_crowd_watching_storm.distinct_from: mockers_wag_heads (close mocking pair) and kneeling_at_cross (kneelers at base) - this is a wide DARK RING of witnesses under storm

tear_track_macro.verse: this one is about me (the personal claim)
tear_track_macro.prompt: an EXTREME MACRO of a single human eye, lash-shadowed, one tear cutting a clean track through dust on the skin, a tiny reflection of a cross in the wet of the eye; intimate; 1st-century
tear_track_macro.distinct_from: cry_face_tears (whole face) - this is ONE EYE ONLY with the cross reflected in it

substitute_shadow.verse: he bore the forsaking in our place (substitution)
substitute_shadow.prompt: a HIGH view at dawn of a small huddled group of ordinary people on pale ground, the long dark shadow of an unseen cross falling across the ground BESIDE them, leaving them standing in clean light; it fell on him, not them; 1st-century
substitute_shadow.distinct_from: kneeling_at_cross (kneeling AT the cross) - here the cross is unseen and its SHADOW spares the people

grave_clothes_folded_macro.verse: John 20:7 - the linen clothes lying folded
grave_clothes_folded_macro.prompt: a MACRO of a single linen cloth folded FLAT into a small neat square lying low on the bare cut stone ledge, the ledge otherwise empty, a shaft of pale dawn light across the weave, dust motes rising; absence as victory; 1st-century
grave_clothes_folded_macro.distinct_from: empty_tomb_open (the whole tomb interior) - this is only the FOLDED LINEN close up

stone_rolled_groove.verse: the stone rolled away (the grave could not hold him)
stone_rolled_groove.prompt: a MACRO along the carved stone groove of a tomb entrance, the great round sealing stone rolled fully OPEN at the groove's end, morning light flooding through the gap it left; the open way; 1st-century
stone_rolled_groove.distinct_from: empty_tomb_open (interior with ledge) - this is the ROLLED STONE in its groove from outside

congregation_hands_lifted.verse: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee (Ps 22:22)
congregation_hands_lifted.arms: many hands lifted high toward the light
congregation_hands_lifted.prompt: a WIDE view from BEHIND a packed congregation of 1st-century worshippers, dozens of hands lifted high toward a warm light source ahead, robes and prayer shawls edge-lit; corporate praise; 1st-century
congregation_hands_lifted.distinct_from: kindreds_bowing (a bowing ring seen frontally) - this is from BEHIND, hands LIFTED not bowed

morning_birds_hill.verse: the hinge from night to morning
morning_birds_hill.prompt: a WIDE view of birds rising in a loose spiral off a rocky hilltop into first light, the empty cross small at the crest, long soft dawn shadows down the slope; release; 1st-century
morning_birds_hill.distinct_from: dawn_empty_cross (static dawn wide) - this one is defined by the RISING BIRDS

threshold_open_door.verse: the congregation it ends in still has room for you (the invitation)
threshold_open_door.prompt: a GROUND-LEVEL view up a worn stone path to an ancient open doorway at dusk, warm firelight and moving shadows of a gathering spilling out across the threshold toward the viewer, the door standing wide; room inside; 1st-century
threshold_open_door.distinct_from: hand_reaching_closeup (the scarred hand) - this is the OPEN DOOR with light spilling out
